newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan brokers chief opposes OTC sale of trust fund.
newsitem.headline: Japan brokers chief opposes OTC sale of trust fund.

text.p: Masashi Suzuki, chairman of the Japan Securities Dealers Association, said on Thursday that he was opposed to Japanese banks selling investment trust products over the counter.

In a speech to a convention of brokerages, he said it was questionable whether it would be right for Japan to revise a law barring Japanese banks from the stock business in order to allow them to offer risky investment trust products.
Industry sources say banks are keen to use their extensive branch networks to directly sell investment trust funds, the equivalent of U.S. mutual funds, to depositors nationwide.

Suzuki also said the securities industry would seriously cope with growing calls for the liberalisation of stockbroking fees. However, he said the issue should be considered in a more comprehensive context, together with discussions on other issues such as corporations' shareholdings which are larger than those of individual investors, and the taxation system on securities investments.

Financial assets held by individuals stood at 1,184 trillion yen at the end of 1995. Of this, only 12 percent or 150 trillion yen is in the form of securities and of this, about 7.0 percent in stocks, he said.
